accepted.s: The National Development Council was set up in August 1952 by means of:
o: A resolution of the Supreme Court

accepted.tq: Distinguish an executive body from constitutional and statutory bodies.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the National Development Council?
accepted.x: The Chairman of the Finance Commission is not a member of the National Development Council. Its membership included the Prime Minister, Union Cabinet Ministers, State Chief Ministers, Union Territory administrators and Planning Commission members.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded member in a composition question.
accepted.sec: National Development Council - composition, status, coordinating role

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Development Council:
1. It approved the draft Five-Year Plans.
2. It linked the Planning Commission with the States.
3. It was intended to meet at least twice a year.
4. It continues to be the active coordinating body under the present institutional arrangement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Council approved draft Five-Year Plans, linked the Planning Commission with the States and was intended to meet at least twice a year. It is presently inactive, with its coordinating role having passed to the Governing Council of NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Reject the present-status trap while retaining the historical functions.
accepted.sec: National Development Council - composition, status, coordinating role

accepted.s: The coordinating role formerly associated with the National Development Council has largely passed to the:
accepted.x: The coordinating role of the National Development Council has passed to the Governing Council of NITI Aayog, while the NDC is inactive.
accepted.tq: Identify the successor institution by its coordinating function.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the difference between the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog regarding financial powers?
o: NITI Aayog allocates plan funds, whereas the Planning Commission had only advisory powers.
The Planning Commission allocated plan funds, whereas NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power and works with the Finance Ministry.
Both allocate plan funds directly to ministries and States.
Neither institution has any relationship with the allocation of public funds.
accepted.x: The Planning Commission allocated plan funds to ministries and States. NITI Aayog has no fund-allocation power and functions in this area along with the Finance Ministry.
accepted.tq: Compare the institutional power rather than the broad policy objectives.
accepted.sec: NITI vs Planning Commission - fund allocation, approach

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly contrasts the approaches of the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog?
1. The Planning Commission followed a top-down approach.
2. NITI Aayog follows bottom-up planning.
3. NITI Aayog is associated with cooperative federalism.
4. The Planning Commission adopted a one-size-fits-all approach.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Planning Commission was associated with top-down, one-size-fits-all plans, whereas NITI Aayog emphasises bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism.
accepted.tq: Use paired opposites in a comparison table to identify the complete combination.
accepted.sec: NITI vs Planning Commission - fund allocation, approach

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Planning Commission — States represented on the Governing Council
NITI Aayog — States’ role limited to annual plan discussions
Planning Commission — Member-Secretary appointed by the Prime Minister
NITI Aayog — States represented on the Governing Council
accepted.x: Under NITI Aayog, States are represented on the Governing Council. Under the Planning Commission, the role of States was limited mainly to the National Development Council and annual plan discussions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State-participation mechanism of the two institutions.
accepted.sec: NITI vs Planning Commission - fund allocation, approach

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the leadership and membership structure of the two institutions:
1. The Member-Secretary of the Planning Commission was appointed through the usual process.
2. The Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog is appointed by the Prime Minister.
3. The Planning Commission had no provision for part-time members.
4. NITI Aayog may have part-time members as needed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the institutional differences: the Planning Commission used the usual process for its Member-Secretary and had no part-time members, while NITI Aayog’s CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister and part-time members may be included as needed.
accepted.tq: Check each institutional contrast independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: NITI vs Planning Commission - fund allocation, approach

accepted.s: A Parliamentary Standing Committee criticised the Ministry of Planning and NITI Aayog for chronic under-use of funds and sought what amount for 2026–27?
accepted.x: The Parliamentary Standing Committee sought ₹1,203.38 crore for 2026–27 while criticising the chronic under-use of funds by the Ministry of Planning and NITI Aayog.
accepted.tq: Distinguish close numerical alternatives by checking the leading and middle figures.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects a recent Andhra Pradesh-related development associated with NITI Aayog and its initiatives?
1. The Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh attended the 11th Governing Council meeting in June 2026.
2. ASR district ranked first nationally on the Basic Infrastructure theme in the March 2026 Aspirational Districts rankings.
3. Andhra Pradesh ranked fifth in the EPI 2024.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister attended the 11th Governing Council meeting in June 2026, ASR district topped the Basic Infrastructure theme in March 2026, and Andhra Pradesh ranked fifth in EPI 2024.
accepted.tq: Combine three state-specific current-affairs facts without confusing their dates or indicators.

accepted.s: Which statement best captures a major criticism of NITI Aayog?
o: It excludes States from all institutional consultations.
It is an advisory body without funds or statutory backing, making its influence on States dependent substantially on persuasion.
It is a statutory body that directly allocates all plan funds to States.
It is a constitutional body with unrestricted power to impose plans on States.
accepted.x: NITI Aayog is criticised for being an advisory body without fund-allocation powers or statutory backing; consequently, its influence on States depends substantially on persuasion.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional features to assess the practical limitation on influence.
